questions.q:
We must/take care of one other/in times of crisis.

(SSC Selection Post phase-XI 27/06/23)
questions.s:
The correct answer is "of one another".

"One other" is incorrect because the correct expression is "one another" when referring to mutual actions or relationships between two or more people.

"One another" is used for reciprocal actions (when people do something for each other).

The corrected sentence should be: "We must take care of one another in times of crisis.

questions.q:
You care for him / even more than for myself, / he cried bitterly.

(SSC CHSL 13/03/2023 S3)
o: even more than for myself
questions.s:
Correct Answer: even more than for myself

  • "myself" is incorrect here. "Myself" is used when the action refers back to the speaker. In this sentence, "me" should be used because the sentence is comparing "him" with "me."

  • Reflexive pronouns (myself, himself, herself, etc.) are used only when the action reflects back to the subject.

  • In comparisons or direct objects, use objective pronouns like me, him, her, etc.

Correct Sentence: You care for him even more than for me, he cried bitterly.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence.
questions.s:
Answer: 1
Solution: The correct substitution is "its".

The sentence becomes:
"The energetic kitten is playful after having its breakfast."
Here, "its" is the correct possessive pronoun used to show that the breakfast belongs to the kitten (उसका नाश्ता).

Option 2 – it’s ❌: contraction of “it is” or “it has”; not possessive.
Option 3 – it ❌: subject pronoun; doesn’t show possession.
Option 4 – it is ❌: a full clause; grammatically incorrect in this context.

Hence, "its" is the most appropriate choice.

questions.q:
Such was the education/of the Spartans with regard to/one of the greatest of there kings.

(SSC CHSL Tier-01 21/03/23)
o: One of the greatest of there kings
Such was the education
Of the Spartans with regard to
questions.s:
The correct answer is Option 2: One of the greatest of there kings.

  • "there" is a possessive determiner (used to show possession), but here it should be "their", which is the correct possessive form to indicate ownership (referring to the kings belonging to the Spartans).

  • "There" is typically used to refer to a place or location (e.g., over there), but in this sentence, "their" is required.

Correct sentence: Such was the education of the Spartans with regard to one of the greatest of their kings.
